profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at Google
profile.summary:
I believe in success through hard work and determination. Collaboration with the right people at the right times is of key importance.

My dream is to become the lead engineer of a team that's in charge of pushing the next technological breakthrough through hardware and software co-design.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Accelerator Platforms & Labs team. Provided low-level software support for Gen5 PCIe switches and retimers. Worked with the hardware engineering team to ensure their design met the software engineering team's requirements for monitoring and diagnosability and repairability.
Designed a continuous validation and firmware release system for these products, for both development and production support.

Designed out-of-band device management daemons for multiple families of products, iteratively improving their architecture and capabilities with each generation. Researched multi-threaded + multi-tasked design patterns and implementations for the OpenBMC platform, leveraging the Boost:ASIO Proactor Design Pattern.

Investigated and root-caused hardware and software reliability issues causing production outages. Identified a set of new telemetry data to automatically monitor, diagnose and suggest repair actions in a data center context reducing the time-to-repair and therefore machine downtime.

Provided software support during new device bring-up. Validated basic operations such as pinging a device for its heartbeat, validating and updating its firmware version, collecting telemetry and asserting baseline functionality.

Created roadmaps for the upbringing of new hire teammates, maintaining a balance of study and implementation tasks of increasing complexity to boost their engagement.
positions.insights: OpenBMC, Embedded Software Design and +5 skills

positions.title: Staff Digital Hardware Engineer
positions.description: Source Measure Unit Design Team: Collaborated with a multi-disciplinary (15+ person) team in the design and development of the following SMU boards: PXIe-4139, PXIe-4162, PXIe-4163, and PXIe-4147. Greatly improved the VHDL simulation performance and code coverage using VHDL2008 features. Certified LabVIEW Developer certification.

positions.title: PXI Embedded Controllers Intern
positions.description: Designed the first prototype of the PXIe-8267 Data Storage Module. Part-selection, board-level design, schematic capture, pin selection, board layout.

positions.title: Timing and Synchronization Hardware Intern
positions.description: I was in charge of developing a new GPS-based timing and synchronization module. Implemented an embedded system which fetches GPS/GLONASS measurements, allows on-the-fly reconfiguration of a GPS/GLONASS IC and interfaces with an existing FPGA design.

certifications.name: Signal Integrity and High Speed System Design
certifications.title: Signal Integrity and High Speed System Design

honors.title: Best Hardware Hack
honors.description:
Worked together with Michael Novén and Andrés Galaviz to implement an internet-based remote-controlled quad-copter drone that could send a live video feed to a webserver, based on existing software frameworks.
http://devpost.com/software/flying-cameraman

volunteerExperiences.description: I worked with a team providing therapeutic play to children recovering in the long-term stay area in order to help reduce their stress, alleviate boredom and let them develop as children their age usually would.
I direct a remote 1h class twice a week teaching high-school students programming and Software Engineering (Agile, Jira, Unit-Testing, etc).

projects.title: Breakout
projects.description: I created my own "Breakout" game in Java, just for fun as a summer project. This was my first Java Swing GUI experiment. Codewise, there's plenty of room for improvement and I've come a long way since then; nevertheless, it's perfectly functional and actually quite fun. I consider this a very important milestone in the development of my skills as a programmer.

projects.title: NUSAnswers.com
projects.description: Created a Quora-like website tailored to the NUS community as part of the final project for my Web Development module at NUS. Michael and I comprised the front-end team. He created most of the UI designs and I wrote most of the AngularJS that supports the client-side application.
